claim: zbus 5.19.0 is a stable, 93.65%-documented pure-Rust D-Bus crate (MIT, published 09 August 2026) that handles connection establishment and message send/receive for method calls, signals and more.
stance_target: zbus is mature enough to be the D-Bus layer for a fleet-wide jupiterOS agent
quoted_support: This is the main subcrate of the zbus project, that provides the API to interact with D-Bus. It takes care of the establishment of a connection, the creation, sending and receiving of different kind of D-Bus messages (method calls, signals etc) for you. Status: Stable.

claim: zbus runs on a broad platform matrix (Linux, FreeBSD, NetBSD, macOS, Windows, Android aarch64-linux-android) and supports vsock and multiple async runtimes (async-io default, tokio optional).
stance_target: zbus can serve D-Bus-style IPC on every host class in the jupiterOS fleet, including non-Linux edge cases, and integrates with a tokio-based agent
quoted_support: aarch64-linux-android, x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, x86_64-unknown-freebsd, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-netbsd ... tokio ^1.37.0 optional ... tokio-vsock ^0.7 optional

claim: The zbus client pattern uses the #[proxy(interface, default_service, default_path)] macro to generate a typed proxy (e.g. MyGreeterProxy) from Connection::session().
stance_target: how ha-linux-agent would consume existing D-Bus services (logind, hostname1, NetworkManager) from Rust
quoted_support: #[proxy( interface = "org.zbus.MyGreeter1", default_service = "org.zbus.MyGreeter", default_path = "/org/zbus/MyGreeter" )] trait MyGreeter { async fn say_hello(&self, name: &str) -> Result<String>; } ... MyGreeterProxy::new(&connection)
